cluster_dependence.text: The benchmark uses one model, 18 hand-constructed cases, six domains, and short JSON assessments rather than full papers. Expected relations are deterministic contracts chosen by the system investigators, not independent expert annotations. The primary McNemar analysis treats case--seed responses as paired observations; dependence among seeds for the same case limits generalization, so domain and leave-one-domain-out summaries are supplied.

Future work should add independently authored cases, multiple models, clustered or case-level inference, standardized Workflow Run RO-Crate export, and external domain review. A scientific agent should be judged by whether its claims survive these checks, not by how many documents it can generate.

raw_responses.text: Scientific-agent systems can execute code and draft papers while still losing the meaning of negative evidence. A.M.Y/Atlas addresses that failure mode as a system problem: a controller delegates computation to an isolated Atlas tool process, records tool outputs with SHA-256 provenance, and packages synthesis requests, raw responses, scores, audits, and manifests as a reviewable release. We evaluate one preregistered claim: whether an explicit evidence policy reduces false support when fixed computational evidence refutes a hypothesis, beyond attaching a hash and provenance identifier alone. The benchmark contains 18 cases in six domains, three synthesis arms, and ten paired model seeds (540 planned outputs). Among 60 complete refuting-evidence pairs, false-support rates were 0.0% for hash-only and 0.0% for the full policy (risk difference 0.0 percentage points, 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.0], exact McNemar p=1); the preregistered hypothesis was therefore not supported. The null result is the point of the artifact: the release keeps the failed hypothesis, raw model outputs, tool coverage gap, and provenance debt inspectable rather than hiding them behind fluent prose. Secondary analysis found unsupported-decimal rates of 37.8%/20.0%, the only endpoint surviving Holm correction (adjusted p=4.532e-05). The paper contributes an auditable evaluation pattern for scientific agents, not a claim that A.M.Y autonomously made a scientific discovery.
1. a preregistered, paired falsification-retention benchmark with immutable raw responses, deterministic scoring, exact tests, confidence intervals, and explicit failure reporting;

For each unique Atlas tool/input pair, the runner stores `output.txt` and `provenance.json`. The provenance record includes the input, success state, duration, environment, and SHA-256 digest of the complete UTF-8 output. Every synthesis request stores the evidence digest and a relative provenance identifier. Requests, raw responses, parsed outputs, and scores are retained separately and joined by a case--arm--seed identifier.

Hosted model behavior can change behind a stable name, making the committed raw responses authoritative and reruns replications rather than exact reproductions. The unsupported-number detector covers decimal forms with tolerance and does not verify every mathematical transformation. Prohibited-claim matching is phrase-based. The Atlas curated audit covers only 24 of 95 registered tools. The historical local census is explicitly nonportable and may contain user-generated artifacts absent from a clean clone.

The release contains the preregistration, frozen case file, protocol record, Atlas evidence and provenance, all model requests and raw responses, parsed scores, analysis tables, figures, manuscript sources, and SHA-256 manifests. Paths are relative to the release root. API credentials and unrelated user artifacts are excluded. The evidence ledger maps primary manuscript numbers to source files and JSON fields.
